plot_local.fact: Thane Hearthless killed Hollow Choir disciple Brother Quell on the Spine Road eleven days ago and harvested his Lagging Shadow power. The Choir has not found the body.
The Choir needs Pip alive and dreaming: each night he dreams in the Quiet Rooms, they map more of the way to Aldrumm's true heart (Choir clock ticks once per day).

BONE-QUAKE (Stirring 4): Rib Row tilted several degrees; sealed Marrow Pit Number Nine collapsed, opening a shaft down toward the heart-cavity. The Hollow Choir now knows exactly where the true heart is: behind a door set in the bone with a lock shaped like an open hand.
Aldrumm felt his grandson die inside his own dream. Three hundred years asleep, and the first thing he has woken enough to feel is grief.

CHOIR CLOCK FULL (dawn, 5th of Harvestwane): the Hollow Choir went down the collapsed shaft of Pit Nine to the heart's door and pressed Thane's dead Hearthblood hand to the lock. The door opened a crack. The Carrion Queen has begun to feed. Across Godbones every marrow lamp is dimming and the bones have begun, very slowly, to grey.

Vane, exposed and burned, moved the Heartstone out of the Chapel reliquary (where to is not yet known) and sent a note to Gristle's shop by a Hollow-sung runner: 'The lamp for the acolyte. Midnight. The Chapel steps. Come alone, little hearth.'

Wenna Tull says at least twelve more Guild children are still Hollow-sung in the Chapel's Quiet Rooms. Brannoc Tull says the Chapel was built by Guild hands three hundred years ago: there is an old coal-and-ash chute from the Chapel kitchens down into the upper Marrow Pits that nobody in the Chapel remembers.
The Heartstone is on Deacon Vane's body, strapped under the burn bandages on her arm. She means to carry it through the heart's door to the Carrion Queen herself.

lore.fact: Thane Hearthless carries Aldrumm's blood (Hearthblood). Nobody in Godbones knows yet.
Pip's word is a Marrowtongue hearth-word (kindling / home-fire). Mother Gristle's cheek scar is the same word, burned in when she learned it.

Thane's Lamp: Thane Hearthless's cracked marrow lamp, now kept by Aldrumm's promise. It never goes out (not for wind, water, or the Carrion Queen). Its light is true hearth-light: the Queen's hymn burns out of anyone standing in it, and the Hollow-sung cannot abide it. Every hearth-fire in Godbones now crackles with Thane's name.

session_events.fact: Deacon Vane, helped by two market porters, is carrying the unconscious Pip up the climb toward the Chapel of the Long Wake. She did not notice Thane's wrist.

Thane spoke Pip's word (a hearth-word of Marrowtongue) untutored in Gristle's doorway, reaching for Aldrumm. Nat 20: Aldrumm answered and paid half the Toll. Gristle's cold stove roared alight and the word-shaped burn scar on her cheek glowed. The Stirring rose to 1.
The Chapel bell stopped. Deacon Vane took Pip into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms. Thane chose to stay and seek a real Marrowtongue apprenticeship from Gristle rather than chase the procession.

Training day two: Thane's first binding-word test misfired (bound his own jaw); he used the Stopping. By evening he was proficient and could bind reliably. At dusk Deacon Ilsabet Vane knocked at the front of Gristle's shop, asking about the stove that relit itself.

Thane reached for Aldrumm a second time to bind Deacon Vane to her oath (cast 18 vs DC 15, success). Calling the god moved the Stirring +2 (now 3/6), crossing 2: tonight the whole town shares a dream of Aldrumm. His blood-oath to Gristle burned him for 6 HP. The Toll came up as Collapse (0 HP); the working is held on his tongue, not yet tied off.

Thane took Gristle's hand to share the Toll: took 18, dropped to 0 HP, failed one death save, and Gristle stabilized him (Medicine 18). Exhaustion 1. The binding HELD: Deacon Vane is compelled to return Pip home, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell. Vane saw Gristle pay half the Toll and now knows Gristle is a Marrowtongue speaker allied with the hidden Hearthblood.

In the shared dream Thane tried to burn Deacon Vane with the hearth-word and invite Aldrumm in (Grand working). Cast 7 vs DC 20: FAILED. The reach still moved the Stirring +2 (now 5/6). His oath burned him for 10 at 0 HP: one death-save failure, no longer stable. The Toll came due in full (death unless shared). Vane saw his face and the vertebrae cord in the dream.

Thane Hearthless, Aldrumm's many-times-grandson, died on a pallet in the back room of Gristle's Pickles & Preserves on the night of the 4th of Harvestwane, Year 302, paying the Toll in full. At the end he let go of Gristle's hand so she would not die with him.

After midnight on the 4th, the Hollow-sung came to Gristle's shop. Gristle held the back door with the binding-word (14 vs 15, failed by one): they broke through the front, took Thane's body, and left Gristle unconscious and badly hurt among the broken jars. She lives.

Answer to Pip's prayer: the grey patch of dying bone by his bed went soft and warm along an old marrow-vein seam. Pip scraped through with his knife (Stealth 17 vs 13), unheard by the Hollow-sung acolyte outside, and dropped into a warm marrow vein leading down toward the heart.

Pip kept his vow at the heart-cavity: Aldrumm woke THROUGH him (cast 20 vs DC 20). The god shared the Toll; Pip collapsed to 0 HP, went 1 success / 1 failure on death saves, and was stabilized by a freed acolyte. THE STIRRING HIT 6: Aldrumm opened one eye. His hearth-fire burned the Carrion Queen's hymn out of the four Hollow-sung (now ordinary, dazed acolytes again). The god pulled Thane's dead hand from the lock and the heart's door slammed shut on the Queen. The grey-robed Choir cantor fled through the crack before it closed. Across Godbones every marrow lamp flared gold and the greying of the bones stopped. The Skull, a day north, unsealed.

Pip stayed hidden in the heart-cavity all day so Vane could not keep her oath, and short-rested (8/15 HP). He sent Acolyte Benedek up to the Chapel to find the Heartstone. Benedek (nat 1) was caught by Deacon Vane within the hour; terrified, he told her Pip was in the heart-cavity with a lamp that would not go out. Vane went for Pit Nine to fetch Pip (search 9 vs 18, failed): the shaft's lip was crowded with Brannoc Tull's Guild crews digging out the quake-trapped, and the hearth-light rising from below would not let her descend.

SUPPER BELL, 5th of Harvestwane: Vane's bound oath broke. The binding Thane tied with Aldrumm's own hand burned her: hearth-fire ran out of her wrist and set her late shadow alight, and the Carrion hymn screamed out of her mouth in front of Brannoc Tull and forty Guild scrapers at the mouth of Pit Nine. Her cover is gone. Badly burned, she fled toward the Chapel.

Evening of the 5th: Pip led three freed acolytes carrying Thane's body up the collapsed shaft of Pit Nine by Thane's Lamp. Wenna Tull slipped and broke her leg (carry check failed); Guild ropes caught her and the body. Brannoc Tull, seeing his missing niece come up out of the god's heart by hearth-light, was warm to Pip (reaction 11) and sent six scrapers with him and Thane's body to Gristle's shop.

Before midnight Gristle taught Pip the Stopping (19 vs 12). At midnight: Gristle went alone to the Chapel steps and kept Deacon Vane talking (Deception 14 vs Insight 11; Vane believes Pip is coming). Twenty Guild men under Brannoc went quiet into the upper pits for the old ash-chute. Pip went up the marrow vein into his old cell (Stealth 24), found Benedek, and held Thane's Lamp to the door grille: the Hollow-sung guard's hymn burned out of him and, weeping and confused, he unlocked the door.

Fight in the Quiet Rooms ward: Pip rigged a drying-line snare (nat 20). His hearth-word at Coyle's grey lamp failed (11 vs 13); he used the Stopping (dull ache, no Toll). Sister Coyle charged at the sound, hit the line at the throat (14 vs 25), went down prone and lost her tuning fork. Thane's Lamp burned her (4) but she resisted blinding (15 vs 12). Pip cut her throat (17 vs AC 12, 6 dmg): wounded, not dead, voice ruined. Her rasped hymn-note failed on him (save 18). Coyle 12/22. The children's humming is faltering without the fork.

Round 2: Pip clubbed Sister Coyle across the head with Thane's Lamp (15 vs AC 12; 2 bludgeoning + 2 hearth-burn). The lamp's glow burned her again (6). She clawed Pip's face (14 vs AC 13, 3 dmg). Coyle is at 2/22, barely conscious, the hymn guttering in her. Pip 5/15. The Guild broke through the kitchen ash-chute wall at the end of the round.

Pip held Thane's Lamp over the dying Sister Coyle (roll 20): the hymn burned out of her and Orla Coyle of Fourth Pit, gone forty years, came back as herself at 1 HP. Pip raised the lamp over the ward and all fourteen Guild children woke from the hymn. The Guild carried them out through the ash-chute. Orla whispered: Vane has the Heartstone strapped under the bandages on her burned arm.

When the Guild brought down the ward wall, Vane knew she'd been played. She struck Mother Gristle down on the Chapel steps with the Carrion hymn (Gristle alive, unconscious, Mallow with her) and ran for Pit Nine with the Heartstone, now that the Guild has left the shaft and Thane's Lamp is no longer below.

player_choices.fact: Thane swore on his Hearthblood to Mother Gristle that when he wakes Aldrumm, he will wake him slow, so the god does not roll over the town. In return she teaches him Marrowtongue.
Pip prayed to Aldrumm for all the hearths of Godbones, asked him for guidance, and offered himself to wake the god when he reaches the heart.
Pip spent the god's promise on Thane: 'Keep the lamp man. Give him his grandson, who died to get me out.' Aldrumm kept it.

plot_world.fact: Aldrumm the Hearthfather is awake, or one eye of him is: a vast amber light now burns in the eye-socket of the Skull, visible from every street in Godbones. He has not moved. Nobody knows what he wants yet.

Aldrumm cannot wake further than one eye without moving, and if he moves, Godbones dies. He asks that the Heartstone (held by the Chapel of the Long Wake) be brought to his heart's door: set in the hand-shaped lock, it will seal the door against the Carrion Queen forever.
